source_basis: Current main-paper titles, subtitles and concise source-bound descriptions in prepare_book.py; bridges describe reading order and do not assert new theorem dependencies.

I.bridge_before: The opening chapter introduces the seed and operator language used throughout the book.
I.bridge_after: The next chapter compares these descriptions across refinement levels and asks which structures survive that passage.

II.bridge_before: The linear framework now becomes a language for comparing resolutions.
II.bridge_after: The next chapter moves from linear packet coordinates to typed nonlinear operations and analytic jets.

III.bridge_before: The preceding constructions provide the linear setting. This chapter studies nonlinear coordinates and the limits of their extension.
III.bridge_after: The next chapter develops a cyclic analytic family through coefficient selection, transport and spectral data.

IV.bridge_before: The focus shifts from the general packet language to a particular analytic family.
IV.bridge_after: The next chapter turns to signals, where filters, packet trees and reconstruction make changes of resolution concrete.

V.bridge_before: The analytic constructions give way to signal representations and reconstruction.
V.bridge_after: The next chapter asks how transfers evolve in time and how eliminated states contribute memory.

VI.bridge_before: Static descriptions now become evolution and conditioning problems.
VI.bridge_after: The next chapter treats quantum seeds, operator grammars and finite effective dynamics.

VII.bridge_before: The transfer viewpoint is now developed in quantum settings with their own algebraic and dynamical assumptions.
VII.bridge_after: The next chapter turns to algorithms, separating exact structural reductions from numerical and hardware questions.

VIII.bridge_before: The earlier packet constructions become inputs to exact compilation and numerical implementation.
VIII.bridge_after: The book then turns to arithmetic, beginning with Euler congruences, completion and dyadic geometry.

IX.bridge_before: The arithmetic sequence begins with congruence identities and the hypotheses needed to extend them.
IX.bridge_after: The next chapter organizes residual seeds and conditional system completion from supplied arithmetic data.

X.bridge_before: The congruence study is followed by a framework for residual seeds and compatible arithmetic descriptions.
X.bridge_after: The next chapter studies local packet geometry and the remaining obligations of arithmetic realization.

XI.bridge_before: The preceding chapter separates the arithmetic objects supplied as inputs from those obtained conditionally. Local packet geometry sharpens the realization questions.
XI.bridge_after: The final chapter gives a conditional route through patching support and Hecke compatibility. The open realization obligations remain separate.

XII.bridge_before: The arithmetic sequence culminates in a conditional argument using patching support, Hecke compatibility and the stated representation-theoretic inputs.
XII.bridge_after: The formal companions at the back of the book describe their own precise coverage. The glossary provides a route back to the principal definitions.

shared_notation: Each chapter specifies its ambient spaces, scalar fields, domains and index sets. A symbol reused elsewhere need not denote the same object.
Read every operator with its stated domain and codomain. A formal identity does not by itself extend an operator to a larger space or supply a continuity hypothesis.
Finite algebra, limits and infinite-dimensional constructions have different assumptions. The passage between them is made only where the text supplies it.
Exact identities and floating-point examples are identified separately. Numerical illustrations retain their stated parameters and ranges.
The glossary points to the chapter-local definitions. Those definitions and their hypotheses take precedence over the short glossary descriptions.
